headline: Taper is complete and the engine is intact. Two runs today, both easy, HR obedient. From here it's travel and logistics — the crossing writes the next chapter.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture a week out from Selånger is exactly what you'd want: running has dropped to short, low-effort shakeouts sitting almost entirely in the easiest zone, while the harder work — the long tempo-heavy session and the durable long runs — is banked in the recent-but-not-too-recent past. Strength held live through the taper with regular short functional sessions rather than tapering to zero, which preserves neuromuscular readiness without adding fatigue. Steps remain genuinely high, so incidental movement is carrying the aerobic baseline while structured running recedes. The DETRAINING load status is a labelling artefact of a deliberate taper, not a fitness signal — recent load has fallen sharply by design, and that's the whole point right now. The only real question the data leaves open is recovery quality heading into a demanding effort, which sits outside training load entirely.
sections.trends: The four-week block still shows a meaningful build over the prior four weeks even with the taper folded in, which tells you the ramp into this event was real before the quiet arrived. Year-to-date against last year the gap is enormous — you're multiples ahead of where you were on the same date in 2025. The shape is a clean pre-event arc: build, peak, taper — unusual for an athlete who normally holds year-round readiness rather than periodising, but entirely coherent given a self-supported crossing on the calendar. This is a deliberate exception to the standing model, not a departure from it.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and its anchoring heart rate are unchanged from the 30-day baseline, which during a taper is the reassuring outcome — you want stability, not gains, this close in. The single hard session on the 25th, with substantial time in Z3 and Z4 at a sharp pace, is the most recent proof the top end is intact and hasn't gone stale during the quiet weeks. Nothing here suggests aerobic erosion; the fitness is parked, not fading.
sections.zones: The recent per-session shapes are textbook taper distribution: today's two runs sat almost entirely in Z1 with only a light Z2 dip, and the shakeouts on the 31st and 28th follow the same low-effort pattern. The one genuine intensity session on the 25th stands apart with real Z3/Z4 time — a deliberate sharpener that would look invisible in a weekly average but is exactly the kind of session you don't want buried. Right now the near-total polarisation toward easy is correct; there's no grey-zone drift to flag, and the intensity that mattered was delivered before the taper deepened.
sections.hr_comparison: Nothing notable — strength sessions logged no HR this block, and the run HR data behaves consistently across sources, with today's easy efforts showing low averages and tight max caps exactly as expected for shakeouts.
sections.calendar: The frequency pattern over the last stretch reads as a controlled wind-down: runs shortening and thinning out while strength stays woven through, rather than an abrupt stop. That's a healthier taper signature than simply ceasing to train — it keeps the body's rhythm and movement patterns live right up to travel. The consistency underneath this (a long unbroken run streak plus a steady strength cadence) is what makes the current quiet read as deliberate rather than as a gap.
sections.personal_bests: No PB relevance this week — the taper is about arriving fresh, not chasing marks, and the current easy-only running gives no window to threaten the standing 5K–Half bests. The one figure worth keeping in mind is the 50K, set at the tail of the 137 km effort; the crossing will effectively rewrite your longest-effort context entirely, in days rather than a single push.

watch_items: Watch how easy-run HR responds once daily pack-loaded efforts stack up — the first few days will reset what "easy" actually costs.
Note whether steps hold through the packing-and-travel window or collapse as logistics peak, as a read on residual movement into the transition.
Track back-to-back leg response over the opening days of the crossing — early durability under cumulative load is the genuine unknown, not fitness.
Keep an eye on whether recovery steadies before departure, given how variable recent nights have looked heading into a sustained demand.
